data.title: HSIF’s Three-Day Slide Puts 22,500-Point Support In Focus
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a negative trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the contract fell below the 23,000-point support level, extending its losses for a third consecutive session on Thursday.

HSIF dropped 418 points to close at 22,808 points after opening at 23,227 points and touching an intraday high of 23,231 points. It later fell to a low of 22,775 points before settling below the key support level. In evening trading, it shed another 49 points to 22,759 points.

RHB Research said the long bearish candlestick indicated that selling pressure remained firmly in control, with the index trading below its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages. Its relative strength index had also slipped further below the 50% level.

The next support levels are seen at 22,500 points and 21,500 points, while resistance is pegged at 23,500 points and 24,000 points.

The research house advised traders to maintain short positions initiated at the Nov 13 closing level of 23,576 points, with the stop-loss threshold lowered to 24,000 points.

data.title: Crypto Selloff Drags Bitcoin To Below US$62,000, Ethereum Near US$1,750
data.description:
Bitcoin slipped below US$62,000 on Nov 20, while Ethereum hovered around US$1,750, as persistent selling pressure, institutional fund outflows and weaker investor sentiment continued to weigh on the cryptocurrency market.

Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, traded at approximately US$61,943, down 1.99% over the past 24 hours, having fluctuated between US$61,375 and US$64,056.

The digital asset has lost more than 13% over the past seven days, reflecting sustained weakness amid broader financial market volatility.

Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency, also remained under pressure, trading at approximately US$1,754, down 0.82% over 24 hours.

The token moved between US$1,735 and US$1,817 during the period, extending its weekly decline to approximately 13%.

The latest downturn comes amid continued withdrawals from cryptocurrency investment products and reduced speculative positioning, as investors reassess their exposure to riskier assets.

Bitcoin futures open interest has declined sharply in recent weeks, while Ethereum has experienced an even steeper contraction, signalling a pullback in leveraged trading activity.

Meanwhile, Citigroup has lowered its 12-month price forecasts for both cryptocurrencies, citing weaker institutional demand following the recent selloff.

With Bitcoin struggling to regain the US$64,000 level and Ethereum remaining below US$1,800, traders are closely monitoring whether buying interest can stabilise prices after the latest wave of selling.

data.title: Offshore Yuan Holds Near 52-Week High Despite Brief Dollar Gains
data.description:
The offshore yuan’s recent decline against the US dollar is likely to be a temporary reaction to thin trading conditions rather than a sign of a broader shift in currency sentiment, according to Investing.com.

The USD/CNH pair rose 0.36% to 6.6925 as of 2.07pm EST on Nov 19, indicating a weaker offshore yuan. However, the pair remained near the lower end of its 52-week range of 6.6422 to 7.1212, reflecting the Chinese currency’s relatively strong position over the past year.

USD/CNH was down 5.97% over the past 12 months, indicating an overall appreciation in the yuan against the dollar. Its gains also held up against broader dollar strength, with the one-week and one-month changes standing at 0.29% and 0.15% respectively.

The latest movement was smaller than declines recorded by other emerging market currencies. The US dollar rose 1.23% against the Mexican peso to 19.0676 and 0.68% against the Brazilian real to 5.9213, while the dollar index edged up 0.05% to 103.838.

Investing.com attributed the yuan’s weakness partly to thin liquidity, noting that the move came without a corresponding increase in onshore trading turnover. This suggested stop-loss orders may have contributed to the decline rather than a fundamental change in market conditions.

Chinese exporters could also provide support when onshore trading resumes, as they typically reduce dollar-selling activity outside local market hours. Their return could increase dollar supply and limit further weakness in the yuan.

Meanwhile, traders have been increasing protection against a potential catch-up decline in the currency following its outperformance during broader dollar strength. However, rising demand for hedging does not necessarily indicate a sustained depreciation trend.

The yuan also remained relatively stable following last week’s Nvidia-related developments, weakening the argument that recent chip-sector headlines were driving its movement.

Investing.com said attempts to link the currency’s decline to Advanced Micro Devices’ (AMD) share price slump were also unconvincing.

AMD shares fell 9.62% to US$479.15 as of 2.07pm EST on Nov 19, following a short-seller report alleging links between the chipmaker and blacklisted Chinese entities. The report also highlighted that more than 20% of AMD’s revenue was billed to China and Hong Kong. The allegations had not been verified and AMD had not responded when the report was published.

A single company’s regulatory concerns were unlikely to drive a currency market with trillions of dollars in daily turnover, with broader risk aversion offering a more plausible explanation for the movement.

The S&P 500 was down 1.62% at 7,204.59, while the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) rose 12.99% to 27.75, reflecting increased market uncertainty.

Investing.com said deeper risk aversion and further dollar gains could eventually translate into genuine depreciation pressure on the yuan. However, the currency’s position near its 52-week strongest levels and the potential return of exporter dollar-selling flows suggest the latest weakness could be short-lived.

The next indicator to watch is whether onshore trading activity confirms the offshore yuan’s decline.

Investing.com

data.title: Wall Street Sinks Over 2% As Anthropic IPO Fails To Revive AI Investor Sentiment
data.description:
Wall Street ended sharply lower on Thursday, with all three major US stock indexes falling more than 2%, as Anthropic’s record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) failed to revive investor enthusiasm for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks.

The S&P 500 fell 147.80 points, or 2.02%, to 7,175.83, recording its sixth consecutive session of losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 550.68 points, or 2.25%, to 23,879.20.

Anthropic shares opened at US$111.50, well above their IPO price of US$83, and climbed as high as US$115 before paring gains to close 17.1% above the offer price. The company’s market valuation briefly exceeded US$2 trillion during its debut.

The IPO, the largest on record, had been widely viewed as a key test of investor appetite for AI-related stocks. However, its strong opening failed to lift broader market sentiment.

“The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St Louis, Missouri.

He cautioned against drawing too much meaning from the stock’s first-day performance, noting that investors were adjusting their portfolios to accommodate the new listing.

Technology stocks remained under pressure, with Nvidia falling 3.3% for its sixth consecutive losing session despite issuing an upbeat revenue forecast. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 7.7% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook disclosed that its affiliated fund had taken a short position in the chipmaker.

Micron and Broadcom each lost 2.1%, while cloud computing infrastructure firms CoreWeave and Nebius fell 6.1% and 9.4%, respectively. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined 2.4%.

In other corporate developments, Palo Alto Networks gained 6.4% after raising its 2027 revenue guidance, while Walmart slipped 1% following a weaker-than-expected annual sales forecast.

Investor attention also turned to the Federal Reserve’s next policy decision following the release of minutes from its October meeting, which indicated concerns about persistent inflation.

Markets were pricing in a 96.4% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the Fed’s December meeting, according to CME’s FedWatch tool.

Investors are awaiting next week’s personal consumption expenditures report, which includes the central bank’s preferred inflation measure. Analysts expect annual core inflation to reach 3.2%, above the Fed’s 2% target.

Market breadth reflected the widespread sell-off, with declining stocks outnumbering advancing issues by 4.37 to one on the New York Stock Exchange and 3.55 to one on the Nasdaq.

Trading volume across US exchanges reached 20.83 billion shares, compared with the 20-day average of 19 billion shares.

data.title: US Stock Markets Rise On Anthropic’s Blockbuster Debut
data.description:
US stocks rose on Thursday as investors awaited Anthropic’s public trading debut, which marks a pivotal moment for the artificial intelligence boom.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.4%, while those on the S&P 500 added 1.1%. Contracts for the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.8% as tech stocks surged.

All eyes are on Anthropic after the Claude maker priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share and expanded its offering to 925 million shares due to strong investor demand. At that price, Anthropic is valued at over $1 trillion, less than the market cap of SpaceX when it went public in June, but still larger than Walmart, Micron, and AMD.

The timing of Anthropic’s IPO coincides with a period of upheaval for the AI trade amid anxieties over safety, the durability of the boom, and an incoming Democratic-led Congress. The market’s response to Anthropic’s debut could set the tone for other companies eyeing the public markets, notably OpenAI — which, according to CEO Sam Altman, still plans to go public.

data.title: Big Caring Caps Busy Bursa Debut With Marginal Gain Over IPO Price
data.description:
Big Caring Group Bhd capped a busy debut on Bursa Malaysia’s Main Market on Nov 19, as the counter closed marginally above its IPO price at RM1.09, as a hefty 572.85 million shares changed hands throughout the trading session.

The pharmacy retail group ended its maiden trading day just one sen, or 0.93%, above its IPO price of RM1.08, after giving up most of its earlier intraday gains.

The opened at RM1.05, three sen below its offer price, with 23.53 million shares traded before recovering to RM1.15 at midday, when trading volume had surged to 407.9 million shares.

However, the counter lost momentum in the afternoon session, eventually settling at RM1.09 despite sustained trading activity.

The listing followed an encouraging response to its IPO, which was oversubscribed by 4.31 times, attracting 29,474 applications for 783.75 million shares from the Malaysian public.

In an exclusive interview with BusinessToday ahead of the listing, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Lee Meng Chuan described the IPO as a natural progression for the business following two decades of expansion.

Big Caring has earmarked RM570.7 million, representing 89.5% of its public issue proceeds, to partially repay bank borrowings, potentially reducing its gearing from 2.8 times to 0.9 times and generating annual interest savings of approximately RM26.3 million.

The group is also targeting 40 to 50 new retail pharmacy outlets annually over the next three to five years, supported by annual capital expenditure of approximately RM18 million.

For its first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, Big Caring recorded net profit attributable to shareholders of RM72.5 million on revenue of RM1.11 billion, with its retail segment contributing RM1.04 billion, or 93.3% of total revenue.

Looking ahead, Lee said organic expansion and strategic acquisitions would remain the group’s two key growth engines as it embarks on its next phase as a publicly listed company.

data.title: Stock Today: MR DIY Gains 1% Despite Lower Earnings Forecasts And Target Price
data.description:
Shares in MR D.I.Y. Group (M) Bhd rose 1%, gaining one sen to RM1.01 at 4.02pm, as investors continued to assess the retailer’s weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings and revised growth outlook.

The counter opened at RM1.00, matching its last adjusted closing price, before reaching an intraday high of RM1.05. It touched a low of RM1.00.

Trading volume stood at 4.2 million shares, with buying interest recorded at 2.19 million shares against selling volume of 701,300 shares. The figures were based on Bursa Malaysia data delayed by 15 minutes.

The share performance came a day after CIMB Securities maintained its BUY recommendation on MR DIY but cut its target price to RM1.35 from RM1.89 following its weaker-than-expected 3Q2026 results.

MR DIY recorded a core net profit of RM127 million for the quarter, down 8.6% year-on-year, while nine-month core net profit fell 2.8% to RM458.7 million.

CIMB Securities attributed the weaker performance to higher operating expenses and margin compression from a less favourable sales mix. Revenue, however, increased 4.8% to RM1.3 billion, supported by store network expansion and higher transaction volumes.

The research house said MR DIY was shifting its focus towards improving existing-store productivity while moderating outlet expansion amid subdued consumer spending and intensifying e-commerce competition.

The group has reduced its FY2026 store opening target to 130 from 155 previously and plans to open about 70 outlets in FY2027. It also intends to refurbish between 200 and 250 existing stores across FY2026 and FY2027.

CIMB Securities lowered its FY2026 to FY2028 earnings per share forecasts by between 9.6% and 11.4%, while reducing its target calendar year 2027 price-to-earnings multiple to 20 times from 27.5 times.

Nevertheless, it maintained its BUY call, citing an attractive valuation and dividend prospects, with projected yields of between 6.4% and 8.2% for FY2027 to FY2029.

data.title: Meta Suspends New Share Structure Following Shareholder Lawsuit
data.description:
Facebook parent Meta has suspended a proposed new share structure championed by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg following a legal challenge by shareholders, the German Press Agency (dpa) reported.

Under the proposal, Meta would have issued an additional non-voting share for every existing share.

Zuckerberg secured approval for the plan several weeks ago, which would have allowed him to sell shares without diluting his control over the company.

The proposal was prompted by a proposed one-off wealth tax in California that would have required residents with assets exceeding US$1 billion to pay five per cent of their wealth in tax. Voters rejected the proposal in early November.

Zuckerberg would have needed to sell shares to raise funds to pay the tax, potentially reducing his voting stake under Meta’s existing share structure.

The Facebook founder controls about 60 per cent of the company’s voting rights, giving him effective control.

According to a statement from Meta’s board, Zuckerberg had threatened to leave California to secure approval for the proposal.

Several shareholders subsequently filed lawsuits in Delaware, where Meta is incorporated, challenging the plan.

A court filing showed that the company had agreed to suspend the share issuance while legal proceedings continue.

The new shares were originally scheduled to be issued in mid-January.

data.title: Stock Today: YTL Power Edges Higher 0.25% Amid Data Centre Regulatory Concerns
data.description:
Shares in YTL Power International Bhd edged up one sen or 0.25% to RM4.01 at 12.05pm, as investors continued to assess regulatory concerns surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) chips and data centre operations.

The counter opened at RM4.00 and traded between RM3.96 and RM4.03, with 7.05 million shares changing hands. Its last adjusted closing price stood at RM4.00.

The marginal gain came amid heightened scrutiny over proposed US restrictions on Chinese access to advanced AI computing infrastructure hosted in overseas data centres, which has raised concerns over potential implications for operators in Malaysia.

In a November 16 research note, MBSB Research said the recent sell-off in YTL Power shares had been excessive, maintaining its BUY recommendation and target price of RM5.98.

The research house said investors should distinguish allegations involving NVIDIA and Singapore-based Megaspeed International from YTL Power’s own data centre operations.

It noted that YTL Power’s principal data centre business largely operates on a colocation model, providing space, power and cooling infrastructure to third-party tenants rather than directly managing their GPU computing systems.

MBSB Research added that a formal clarification from YTL Power could help address investor concerns surrounding the allegations.

The proposed US regulations could tighten oversight of advanced AI processors, including NVIDIA’s Blackwell-generation chips, by requiring greater disclosure of customers, chip deployment and intended applications.

However, MBSB Research cautioned against interpreting the proposals as a blanket restriction on data centre development in Malaysia, adding that conventional cloud computing, colocation and enterprise data centre demand from unaffected customers should remain comparatively less exposed.

data.title: Stock Today: Inari Amertron Rallies 6.31% After Stronger 1QFY2027 Earnings
data.description:
Shares in Inari Amertron Bhd rose 13 sen or 6.31% to RM2.19 at 11.18am, following the semiconductor group’s stronger first-quarter financial performance.

The stock opened at RM2.11 and climbed to an intraday high of RM2.24, compared with a low of RM2.09. It was trading 13 sen above its last adjusted closing price of RM2.06, with 7.42 million shares changing hands.

The share price advance came a day after Inari reported a 20% year-on-year increase in profit after tax (PAT) to RM60.4 million for the first quarter ended September 30, 2026 (1QFY2027), from RM50.3 million a year earlier.

Revenue rose 13.1% to RM368.5 million from RM325.8 million, supported by higher loading volumes across all business segments.

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue increased 27.5% from RM288.9 million, while PAT surged more than elevenfold from RM5.3 million in the preceding quarter. The earnings recovery was partly attributed to the absence of a one-off provision of approximately RM41.9 million relating to a fire at its wholly-owned subsidiary in the Philippines.

The board also proposed a first interim exempt dividend of 1.00 sen and a single-tier dividend of 0.50 sen per ordinary share for the financial year ending June 30, 2027.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower, Fed Minutes Keep Rate Hike Concerns Alive
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its losses on Thursday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI falling despite stronger-than-expected third-quarter economic growth and expectations of sustained data centre investment through 2030.

Investor sentiment remained cautious following the release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve’s October policy meeting, which showed policymakers remained concerned about inflation and left the possibility of further interest rate hikes in 2027 open.

At 9.05am, the FBM KLCI had shed 8.42 points to 1,566.73, extending its recent decline after failing to sustain an earlier technical rebound.

Overnight, Wall Street also ended on a mixed note, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 1.11% while technology shares staged a cautious recovery, supporting the Nasdaq.

Apex Securities said the FBM KLCI remained under bearish pressure after breaking below the critical 1,580 support level, with the latest decline reinforcing its prevailing downtrend.

The research firm identified immediate support at 1,550, followed by stronger support at 1,540. A recovery above 1,580 could provide near-term relief, although resistance remains at 1,600 to 1,620, followed by stronger resistance at 1,650.

“Overall, the near-term technical outlook remains bearish, with a meaningful improvement in sentiment contingent on the index reclaiming the 1,650 level,” it said in a note.

Banking stocks led the declines, with Hong Leong Bank falling 14 sen to RM20.96, AmBank Group shedding nine sen to RM6.50 and CIMB Group Holdings losing three sen to RM7.

Among other heavyweights, SD Guthrie declined nine sen to RM5.88, Gamuda fell seven sen to RM4.52 and Press Metal Aluminium Holdings slipped nine sen to RM6.56.

Meanwhile, Big Caring Group Bhd made its Main Market debut at RM1.05, three sen below its IPO price of RM1.08. The stock was heavily traded, ranking as the second most active counter at the time of writing.

data.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar On Stronger 3Q GDP Growth
data.description:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and major currencies on Thursday, supported by improved sentiment following Malaysia’s stronger-than-expected economic growth in the third quarter of 2026.

At 8am, the local currency strengthened to 4.1120/1175 against the greenback from Wednesday’s close of 4.1130/1180.

However, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit could remain under pressure and continue its downward trend ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) December meeting.

He said other Asian currencies had also come under pressure following US retail sales data, which showed a 0.2% month-on-month increase in October, while the Fed’s hawkish stance continued to support the US dollar.

“New York Fed President John Williams explicitly warned that the Fed needs to raise interest rates in order to curb higher inflation,” he told Bernama.

Mohd Afzanizam also noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.28% to 103.773 at the time of writing.

Bank Negara Malaysia reported on Wednesday that the economy expanded by 5.5% in 3Q 2026, compared with 5.3% in the corresponding quarter last year, driven by sustained household spending, higher investment activity and stronger exports.

The central bank said export growth strengthened further, supported by technology-related shipments across electrical and electronics as well as non-E&E products.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit rose against the Japanese yen to 2.5798/5834 from 2.5826/5859, strengthened against the British pound to 5.4056/4129 from 5.4172/4238 and edged higher against the euro to 4.5117/5177 from 4.5144/5199.

Against regional peers, the local currency edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1891/1936 from 3.1896/1937 and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1012/1235 from 12.1138/1339.

It was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 225.5/225.9 and remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.45/6.47.

data.title: Stock Picks: Cnergenz And Northeast Group
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) sees further upside potential in Cnergenz Bhd and Northeast Group Bhd following recent bullish price movements, with both counters showing signs of renewed buying interest.

For Cnergenz, RHB Research said the stock could resume its upward movement after rebounding sharply from its recent low. The counter formed a long bullish candlestick on higher trading volume yesterday and was testing its immediate resistance at RM1.05.

A decisive close above this level would confirm the bullish setup, potentially sending the stock towards RM1.12, followed by RM1.18. However, a fall below the RM1 support would invalidate the rebound and expose the counter to further correction.

Meanwhile, Northeast Group has staged a strong recovery after bouncing off its interim support. The stock formed a Bullish Marubozu candlestick yesterday and closed at its daily high above the RM0.94 resistance, indicating renewed buying momentum.

RHB Research noted that the counter remains below its 21-day simple moving average (SMA), with a move above the line expected to strengthen its bullish outlook.

Following the breakout above RM0.94, Northeast Group could test RM1.02, followed by RM1.10. A decline below the RM0.86 support, however, would negate the bullish setup and signal a resumption of its correction phase.
